reasoning: The window is real. AtomicFileWrite.swift:19 writes the temp file with the default mode, and the chmod to 0600 only comes at :20-24. But the only secret-bearing write another local user could reach is the Codex write-back (FileCredentialReader.swift:74), and that path is not reachable in the default deploy. OpenAIProvider.swift:76 and :92 call refresh/writeBack only when manageOAuthRefresh is true. That flag defaults to false in AppConfig.swift:309/326/350/364 and in the provider init parameters (OpenAIProvider.swift:38/49), and CLAUDE.md treats read-only as a hard rule. The other 0o600 callers (ConfigLoader.swift:110/189/276, DiskCache.swift:135, UsageHistoryStore.swift:152, OpenAIResetJournal.swift:30) write into the app's Application Support and Caches dirs, which the app forces to 0700, so another user cannot get to their temp files; the finding admits this itself. The claimed attack also stacks unproven conditions: a multi-user Mac, a ~/.codex that others can traverse (nothing in the repo sets this dir's mode, so its permissions are not shown), and winning a race window of microseconds. The attacker's source is not reachable in the standard configuration, so the attack path is incomplete.
